findings.title: get_monitor_environment_context returns the un-modified monitor.config instead of the local copy it built
findings.body: The function builds a local `config` by copying `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, then conditionally rewrites `config["schedule_type"]` to the human-readable display string via `monitor_environment.monitor.get_schedule_type_display()`. The return dict, however, uses `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` — the original dict — discarding the local `config` entirely. Consequence: every occurrence event published to Kafka contains the raw `schedule_type` enum value (e.g. `"crontab"`) in the monitor context instead of the localized display string ("Every minute", "Every hour", etc.) the surrounding evidence display strings use. Downstream issue/event UIs that read this context will render the wrong/ugly value for `schedule_type`. The return should use the local `config` variable. This bug existed in the pre-refactor `mark_failed.py` and was carried over unchanged into the new module.
